title: Between frequencies and frustration: The subjective impact of ultrasound examinations on the day-to-day work of nursing staff in German neonatal (intensive care) units
summary: Background: Ultrasound is being used increasingly frequently in wards that care for unwell newborns and premature babies. It helps to detect conditions at an early stage without causing the children any pain. The examinations often take place right at the bedside, thereby altering the workflow on the ward. Nursing staff are involved in many of these examinations, for example by preparing for them, positioning the babies or liaising with doctors. How this affects nurses’ day-to-day work has hardly been studied to date. Research question: We wish to find out how nursing staff on neonatal wards in Germany experience the use of ultrasound in their day-to-day work. We are interested in whether and to what extent it influences the flow of care, and whether it is perceived as a relief, an additional burden, or both. Methodology: We are conducting a Germany-wide survey amongst nursing staff on neonatal wards. Participants will complete a questionnaire about their personal experiences. Participation is voluntary and anonymous; therefore, no conclusions can be drawn about individual participants. The results will be analysed and published in a scientific journal.

interventions.name: Questionnaire survey of neonatal nurses across Germany

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
a qualified nurse who, at the time of the survey, was also working in a neonatal unit in Germany (Level 1–3).
Exclusion criteria:
Unqualified nursing assistant, working outside the neonatal unit
